column2: Debian apt archive, full delivery (build step 7; the write-triggered-services-prototype precedes it and this spec must build on its findings rather than repeat them). Ground against the Debian repository format (wiki.debian.org/DebianRepository/Format) and apt's documentation: dists/<suite>/ and pool/ layout, Release/InRelease/Release.gpg, Packages and its compressed forms, Contents, Translation, by-hash (Acquire-By-Hash), Valid-Until, components and architectures, source packages. Real client: apt inside a debian container via `podman` or `docker` if available. Proxied: mirroring deb.debian.org where Release is mutable and pool files immutable; signatures on proxied content are the upstream's, but a hosted or merged repository must be re-signed by us, via the shared signing service. Hard traps: repository-wide regeneration on every publish, concurrent publishes, Valid-Until expiry on a served snapshot, and the by-hash layout interacting with CAS.

RPM repositories for dnf/yum (RHEL, Fedora, SUSE, Rocky, Alma), full delivery. Ground against the createrepo_c documentation and the repodata format: repomd.xml, primary/filelists/other XML (gzip and zstd), repomd.xml.asc, gpgcheck vs repo_gpgcheck, updateinfo, comps groups, modules metadata. This host runs Fedora, so `dnf` is a real client available locally: use it against a local probe. Hard traps: repomd.xml is a generated signed index (write-triggered, signed-index class), metadata checksums in repomd, package signatures vs repo metadata signatures being separate trust layers, and zypper differences.

Cargo (Rust) registries. Ground against the Cargo book's registry documentation: the sparse index protocol (config.json, per-crate index files with the 1/2/3/ab/cd path sharding, the `sparse+` URL scheme), the Web API (publish PUT /api/v1/crates/new with its length-prefixed binary body, yank/unyank, owners, search), `Authorization` token auth, `registry.auth-required`, and credential providers. Check `which cargo`. Notable: `cargo yank` is a real client-driven management operation, unlike pip, which matters for docs/internal/analysis/management-surfaces-and-the-oracle.md. Hard traps: the index file per crate is an append-only generated document (write-triggered), name normalisation (hyphen/underscore equivalence and case), and the git index protocol, which you should decide whether to support.

RubyGems. Ground against the RubyGems compact index spec (/versions, /info/<gem>, /names, with the checksums and Range/ETag semantics), the legacy full index (specs.4.8.gz, latest_specs, prerelease_specs, Marshal.4.8 quick specs), the push API (POST /api/v1/gems, Authorization header API key), yank, and Bundler's resolution. Check `which gem bundle`. `gem yank` is client-driven. Hard traps: /versions is an append-only file clients fetch with Range requests, so a proxy must preserve byte-offset semantics; Marshal-format legacy indexes are a deserialisation hazard.

Composer (PHP). Ground against the Composer repository documentation: packages.json, metadata-url (/p2/%package%.json and ~dev variant), the v1 provider-includes legacy format and whether to serve it, available-packages, dist archives vs source references, and how private repositories are typically served (Satis, artifact repositories, Private Packagist). Check `which composer`. There is no standard publish API in the Composer ecosystem: the management surface question applies. Hard traps: metadata minification (the __unset keys in /p2 files), dist URL rewriting on the proxied path, and source references pointing at VCS the registry cannot cache.

Conda channels. Ground against the conda channel layout and CEPs: channeldata.json, <subdir>/repodata.json (and .zst, and CEP-16 sharded repodata), current_repodata.json, .conda vs .tar.bz2 packages, noarch. Clients: conda, mamba, pixi (check `which`). Repodata is a generated, subdir-wide index (write-triggered) that can be very large (CAS-backed metadata). There is no standard upload API (anaconda.org's is proprietary): management-surface question. Hard traps: repodata patching (channel-level metadata hotfixes), and conda-forge scale on the proxied path.

Alpine apk repositories. Ground against the Alpine wiki and apk-tools documentation: APKINDEX.tar.gz, its signature file (.SIGN.RSA.<keyname>.rsa.pub prepended as a tar segment), per-package .apk signing, abuild, and repository/architecture layout. Client: apk inside an alpine container via podman or docker. Signed-index class: the index must be re-signed on every publish via the shared signing service. Hard traps: the concatenated-gzip-stream signature layout, and trusted keys that clients must install.

Conan (C/C++) remotes. Ground against Conan 2 documentation and the conan_server / Artifactory Conan REST API (v2 paths with recipe and package revisions RREV/PREV, conan remote login returning a token). Check `which conan`. Hard traps: revisions as a first-class immutability model, package IDs derived from settings and options, and the v1/v2 API split.

Swift packages. Ground against the Swift Package Registry specification (SE-0292 and the registry.md service spec in the swift-package-manager repository): list releases, fetch release metadata, manifest, source archive, identifiers lookup by URL, the publish endpoint, package signing (SE-0391). Check `which swift`. The catalogue files Swift under a "Git-backed" family; the registry protocol is its own HTTP protocol, so spec it on its own terms and state how it relates to Git-based resolution. Hard traps: scope.name identifiers and case-insensitivity, the Content-Version header, and signature formats.

Pub (Dart and Flutter). Ground against the hosted pub repository specification v2 (github.com/dart-lang/pub/blob/master/doc/repository-spec-v2.md): package listing, archive URLs, the three-step publish flow (GET versions/new, multipart upload, finalize), `dart pub token add` authentication with its WWW-Authenticate handling, retraction and discontinuation. Check `which dart flutter`. Hard traps: archive_sha256, retracted versions and their resolution semantics, and the publish flow's redirect-to-upload shape on the proxied vs hosted path.

Hex (Elixir and Erlang). Ground against the Hex repository specification (github.com/hexpm/specifications): /names, /versions, /packages/<name> as gzipped, signed protobuf payloads, the repository public key, the tarball format (outer checksum), and the Hex HTTP API for publish and retire. Check `which mix rebar3`. Signed-index class: the registry resources are signed by the repository key, so a hosted repository needs the shared signing service. Hard traps: signed protobuf, outer vs inner checksums, retirement semantics.

CRAN-like R repositories. Ground against R's documentation for repositories and install.packages: src/contrib/PACKAGES (plain, .gz, .rds), binary trees under bin/windows/contrib/<R version>/ and bin/macosx/, the Archive/ directory for superseded versions, and tools like drat and miniCRAN as prior art. Check `which R Rscript`. There is no publish API: management-surface question. PACKAGES is a generated index per tree (write-triggered). Hard traps: binaries keyed by R minor version and platform, and Archive/ semantics on the proxied path.

Terraform and OpenTofu registries. Ground against the published protocols: service discovery (/.well-known/terraform.json), the module registry protocol (versions list, download with X-Terraform-Get), the provider registry protocol (versions, download metadata with SHASUMS, its GPG signature and the signing keys), and separately the provider network mirror protocol, which is a different protocol. Check `which tofu terraform`. IMPORTANT prior art in the owner's own codebase: /home/m/code/stackweaver implements a registry (backend/internal/services/registry/, backend/internal/api/v2/handlers/registry_artifact_token.go, and HandleServiceDiscovery in backend/internal/api/routes/routes.go). Read it and say what carries over. Hard traps: provider signing keys and the SHA256SUMS signature, the root-anchored well-known path (see format-handler-interface.md's Mount), and module sources that are VCS URLs rather than archives.

Vagrant boxes. Ground against Vagrant's documentation for box metadata JSON (name, versions, providers with url, checksum and checksum_type, architecture) and `vagrant box add` with a metadata URL, plus the HCP Vagrant Registry API as prior art for publishing. Check `which vagrant`. Hard traps: multi-gigabyte box files (streaming, resumable download), the architecture field added in Vagrant 2.4, and the metadata document being a generated per-box index.

Chef cookbooks. Ground against the Chef Supermarket API (/universe, /api/v1/cookbooks, versions and download endpoints) and how Berkshelf and knife consume it. Check `which berks knife chef`. Hard traps: /universe is a single generated repository-wide dependency document (write-triggered), and cookbook upload uses Chef's signed-request authentication, which must be reconciled with auth.md.

Puppet modules. Ground against the Puppet Forge API v3 (/v3/modules, /v3/releases, file downloads, the release publish endpoint with API key auth) and how `puppet module install` and r10k consume it. Check `which puppet r10k`. Hard traps: author-name module naming, deprecation and deleted-release semantics.

LuaRocks. Ground against the LuaRocks documentation for rocks servers: the manifest (a Lua table, and the versioned manifest-5.x files, plus zip variants), .rockspec and .rock files, and `luarocks-admin make-manifest`. Check `which luarocks`. Hard traps: the manifest is Lua source a server generates (never evaluate uploaded Lua server-side), and per-Lua-version manifests.

Hackage (Haskell). Ground against Hackage's documentation and hackage-security: the index tarball (01-index.tar.gz, incremental, with its append-only semantics) and The Update Framework metadata (root.json, timestamp.json, snapshot.json, mirrors.json) that cabal verifies. Check `which cabal ghcup`. This is the only format in the catalogue with TUF: say how TUF metadata is produced and rotated by the shared signing service, and what a proxy may and may not re-sign. Hard traps: the append-only index and its incremental download, TUF key roles and expiry.

CPAN (Perl). Ground against the CPAN mirror layout (modules/02packages.details.txt.gz, authors/id/X/XX/XXXX/, authors/01mailrc.txt.gz, modules/03modlist.data.gz) and DarkPAN prior art (Pinto, OrePAN2, CPAN::Mini). Clients: cpanm, cpan (check `which cpanm cpan`). There is no standard upload API (PAUSE is bespoke): management-surface question. Hard traps: 02packages is a generated index mapping packages to distributions, and module-to-distribution indexing permissions.

opam (OCaml). Ground against the opam repository format documentation: the repo file, packages/<name>/<name.version>/opam files, index.tar.gz for HTTP repositories, and `opam admin index` / `opam admin cache`. Check `which opam`. The catalogue files opam under "Git-backed"; HTTP repositories exist and are the registry-shaped path, so spec that and state the Git relationship. Hard traps: opam files reference upstream source URLs with checksums rather than hosting archives, so decide what hosting and caching mean.

Julia packages. Ground against the Julia Pkg server protocol (PkgServer.jl and the Pkg documentation: /registries, /registry/<uuid>/<tree-hash>, /package/<uuid>/<tree-hash>, /artifact/<tree-hash>, content addressed by git tree hash, JULIA_PKG_SERVER). Check `which julia`. Registries themselves are Git repositories (General); the catalogue files Julia under "Git-backed". Spec the Pkg server protocol as the registry path. Hard traps: tree-hash content addressing, which differs from our CAS digest, and artifacts.

Homebrew bottles. Ground against Homebrew documentation: bottles are OCI artifacts hosted on ghcr.io with annotations, HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN and HOMEBREW_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN for mirrors, the JSON API (formula.jws.json, cask.jws.json, signed), and taps as Git repositories of formulae. Check `which brew`. State how much of this is already covered by oci.md and what is genuinely new. Hard traps: the signed JWS API documents, and the bearer-token dance ghcr.io requires even anonymously.

Open VSX (editor extensions). Ground against the Open VSX registry API (the /api namespace and extension endpoints, the VS Marketplace compatible /vscode/gallery query endpoint, .vsix downloads, publishing with `ovsx` and a personal access token, namespace ownership and verification). Clients: VSCodium and VS Code configured for a custom gallery (check `which ovsx code codium`). Hard traps: the gallery query endpoint's POST body semantics, namespace ownership as an authorization model, and target platforms.

Arch Linux pacman repositories. Ground against pacman and repo-add documentation: <repo>.db (a tar of desc files, symlinked to .db.tar.*), <repo>.files, .pkg.tar.zst packages with detached .sig, optional database signing, and SigLevel. Client: pacman inside an archlinux container via podman or docker. Signed-index class. Hard traps: repo-add regenerating the db on every publish (write-triggered), and package vs database signature trust.
